seed: Objects of type `target` under action ACTION3 with touching neighbours [reflection] show mixed outcomes: h,pixels,w,y x1, h,pixels,w,x,y x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the exact click position relative to the object, when the action is a click. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Mirror-axis game: horizontal wall axis plus 3x3-cell pieces. Action 5 cycles the selection axis -> piece_0 -> piece_1 -> axis. Actions 1-4 move the selection one cell (3px); the axis only moves along its normal.
Each piece cell is mirrored across the axis centre row as a gray reflection cell (clipped to 63x63). Layers: wall1 < target2 < reflection3 < piece4. A cell centre shows whatever lies beneath; if nothing does, it shows 0 (selected piece) or 4 (reflection). Wall dots are 0 only while the axis is selected.
The objects are re-extracted from the rendered frame. Walls, pieces and reflections are 4-connected components; targets are one object per sprite, occlusion-cropped. Names are sorted by (x,y); wall_h index is offset by the count of black piece pixels.
Hypothesis resolved: the mixed target h/w/x/y/pixels outcomes under ACTION3 are not caused by click position. They come from a reflection occluding the target, and the render+extract step reproduces them.
Unconfirmed (not observed)
